key: Lamb et al. key: Fuss et al. (2018) — 'Negative emissions—Part 2: Costs, potentials and side effects', Environmental Research Letters 13:063002 || The IPCC AR6 WGIII (2022) substantially updates these potential ranges: DACCS potential is now assessed at 5–40 GtCO2/yr (vs 0.5–5 in Fuss 2018), and the AR6 TS gives cumulative BECCS of 328 (168–763) GtCO2 and DACCS of 29 (0–339) GtCO2 across 2°C scenarios. The State of CDR 3rd Edition (June 2026) gives a central range of 7–9 GtCO2/yr total CDR needed by 2050 in Paris-compatible scenarios, with a highest-ambition median of 8.8 GtCO2/yr. The 2046–2056 net-zero CO2 timing range is from a 2018 scenario review and has been superseded by AR6 scenario analysis
